drhp.business: Mangalam Drugs and Organics Ltd. manufactures and sells Active Pharmaceutical Ingredients (API) across therapeutic segments including Anti-Malaria, Anti-Retroviral and Anti-Hypertensive. It is the only API company globally to qualify under the Bill Clinton Foundation for supply of Anti-Malarial drugs, and its revenue is largely dependent on procurement tenders floated by global health agencies for malaria, tuberculosis and HIV treatment programs in developing and under-developed countries.

risks.note: Approximately 65%-70% of revenue depends on procurement tenders floated by global health agencies (Global Fund, UNICEF, UNITAID, USAID) for malaria, tuberculosis and HIV treatment programs; the funding mechanism for these tenders has been severely disrupted by geopolitical and macroeconomic developments and sovereign budget re-prioritization.

The complete disbandment of USAID in December, historically a major contributor to global healthcare funding and a key donor to the Global Fund, led to funding gaps and deferment of procurement decisions, causing a sharp decline in tender issuance across the Company's malaria and tropical disease segments.

As a consequence of the funding disruption, the Company experienced order deferrals, reduced tender participation, and temporary under-utilization of manufacturing capacity, leading to stress on cash flows and working capital cycles — the first such downturn faced by the Company in over 50 years of operations.

The Company is subject to laws and regulations in diverse areas including trademarks, copyright, patents, competition, employee health and safety, the environment, corporate governance, listing and disclosure, employment and taxes; frequent changes in the legal and regulatory regime and multiple regulating authorities add compliance complexity.
